solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Influential prisoner with no answer to reprimand

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war

indicators.note: with no tells us a letter is dropped from the word for a telling-off

parts.note: an earful is a scolding or reprimand

explanation.surface: A powerful inmate who escapes being told off because he never answers back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone influential wields a great deal of power, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Extra large detective turning up wearing extra large yellow floral items

indicators.note: wearing means one set of letters is put on, so placed inside, the other

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, another way of saying extra large
XL is the clothing size label for extra large

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the detective's letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A big detective turns up dressed in plus-size yellow clothes with a flower print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' suits a down clue, where the letters read upwards; 'wearing' then puts the result inside the outsize label.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxlips are pale yellow primrose-like wild flowers, so they fit as yellow floral items.

clue.text: English reduced fat cream

parts.note: lite is the food label for low-fat or reduced-fat products

explanation.surface: A shopping-list note about a low-fat English dairy cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of society means its best members, the select group at the top.

clue.text: Show disapproval, suppressing distressed gasp — jellied eggs?

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something down within, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to frown is to show disapproval

indicators.note: distressed means damaged or roughed up, so the letters of gasp are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone frowns and stifles a horrified gasp when served eggs in jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' is the anagram signal, not an emotion; 'suppressing' holds the scrambled letters within the scowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogs lay their eggs in masses of clear jelly, hence the playful question-marked description.

clue.text: Lecturer, nocturnal type, providing escape finally for criminal

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lecturer, as on learner plates
an owl is a night creature, a nocturnal type
providing means if, as in a condition

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word escape

explanation.surface: A night-owl lecturer helps a criminal get away.
explanation.definitionFit: A lowlife is a disreputable person, often a petty crook, so it fits a criminal.

clue.text: Smart society babywear

parts.note: a nappy is what a British baby wears, called a diaper in the US

explanation.surface: A trendy line of designer clothes for babies.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy describes something stylish and neat, as in a snappy dresser, which is smart.

clue.text: Wobbly, with more than one wine knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means the wines are sent backwards, read in reverse

parts.note: ports are fortified wines, the plural giving more than one

explanation.surface: Someone goes unsteady after downing several glasses of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wobbly' is British slang for a tantrum (to throw a wobbly), not unsteadiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A strop is a bad-tempered sulk or tantrum, the same as a wobbly in British slang.

clue.text: Eat brains fried? I'd rather not

indicators.note: fried means cooked up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Offered a plate of fried brains, a diner politely declines.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains declines to take part, the kind of person who says they would prefer not to.

clue.text: Bar backing Scottish team losing final to Italian

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so backing

indicators.note: losing final means the last letter of the team name is dropped

parts.note: Hibs is the nickname of Hibernian, an Edinburgh football club
It is short for Italian, as in gin and It (Italian vermouth)

explanation.surface: A pub supporting a Scottish side that lost a final to an Italian club.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to forbid it, the same as to outlaw it.

clue.text: Colourless character released on bail

indicators.note: released means set free, so the letters are let loose and reordered

explanation.surface: A dull suspect gets out of jail on bail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colourless character' suggests a boring person, but means one lacking pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: An albino lacks skin and hair pigment, a literally colourless person.

clue.text: Joint project to earn money and spend it?

parts.note: to work is to earn money
to shop is to spend money

explanation.surface: A shared scheme to make money and then splash it out.
explanation.definitionFit: A workshop is a group session where people collaborate on a shared task or study.

clue.text: American journalists at heart liking R and R in Davos?

parts.note: the press means journalists collectively

indicators.note: at heart points to the central letters of the word liking

explanation.surface: American reporters secretly enjoying rest and relaxation at a Swiss resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Davos is a Swiss ski resort; R and R means rest and recreation.
explanation.definitionFit: After-skiing socialising is the rest and recreation people enjoy at a ski resort such as Davos.

clue.text: Quiet Conservative held in check

indicators.note: held in means the party letter is kept inside the cloth

parts.note: plaid is a checked tartan cloth

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician kept silent and restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means calm and peaceful, which is quiet in temperament.

clue.text: A trained cat's cultivated plant

indicators.note: cultivated means worked over like soil, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-trained cat has a refined, cultured manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradescantia, the spiderwort, is a genus of popular houseplants.

clue.text: Object is to adopt children

parts.note: to take in, as with a child, is to adopt
issue means offspring or children

explanation.surface: A statement of a couple's goal to adopt children.
explanation.definitionFit: To take issue with something is to disagree with it, to object.

clue.text: Bovine foodstuff, formed into a mass and battered

parts.note: cud is the food a cow chews again
gelled means set into a jelly-like mass

explanation.surface: A description of cattle feed congealing into a lump, then coated in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' pretends to be cooking batter; it means beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hit repeatedly with a club is being beaten, which is battered.

clue.text: For example, grade one conciseness mostly set back by prolixity

indicators.note: set back means the assembled letters are reversed

parts.note: A is a top school grade
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: mostly means only the first part of the word is kept

parts.note: brevity means conciseness

explanation.surface: A grade A essay for brevity, undermined by wordiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims BREVITY to BREV; 'set back' turns EGAIBREV around.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbiage is excessive wordiness, exactly what prolixity means.

clue.text: 'Kiss me quick'? That's rank

definitions.meaning: a request for a quick kiss, read as an order for a peck
a hierarchy or ranking of status within a group

explanation.walkthrough: Kiss Me Quick hats are seaside souvenirs; read literally the phrase is an order for a peck.
explanation.definitionFit: The hierarchy among hens decides who pecks whom, hence social ranking generally.

clue.text: 0-0, two places above bottom, is worrying

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom letter climbs two positions up the column

parts.note: the score 0-0 read as O minus O

explanation.surface: A goalless draw, with the team second from relegation, is a cause for concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two places above bottom' is a football table phrase; here the final O of OMINUSO rises two places.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ominous threatens trouble, so it is worrying.

clue.text: Pressure from lover leaving note

indicators.note: leaving means the note departs from the word for a lover

parts.note: a mistress is a lover
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: The strain of a lover walking out, leaving only a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental or physical strain, the same as pressure.

clue.text: Do a favour to returning soldier in joint without wife

indicators.note: returning means everything assembled is read backwards
in means the soldier goes inside the shortened joint
without means the wife's letter is taken away

parts.note: the elbow is an arm joint
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Helping out a soldier coming home to a pub with no wife in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like a pub but is a body joint; 'without' removes the wife, 'in' places the soldier, and 'returning' reverses the lot (EGILBO).
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to help them out, which is doing them a favour.

clue.text: Consumed 14 with no starter

indicators.note: with no starter means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: refers to the answer to 14 down, meaning struck with a club

explanation.surface: A beaten opponent swallowed up, with no first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Food consumed has been eaten, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: To kill fish, move around on surface of water

definitions.text: move around on surface of water

parts.note: to ice someone is slang for killing them
a skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A grisly instruction to kill a fish and then circle the pond.
explanation.walkthrough: The water's surface is frozen, which is why this is gliding on blades.
explanation.definitionFit: Skating glides over ice, the frozen surface of water.

clue.text: It's understood North Korea's leaders may receive their currency from the South

indicators.note: in a down entry from the South means read upwards, so reversed
may receive means the money goes inside the two initials
leaders means the opening letters of North and Korea's

parts.note: the won is the currency of Korea

explanation.surface: A remark that North Korean leaders may get funds from South Korea.
explanation.walkthrough: NK takes in WON to give NWONK; 'from the South' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something understood is known, a matter of common knowledge.

clue.text: High-pitched argument follows taking out of rubbish

indicators.note: follows means the argument comes after the shortened rubbish
taking out means removing a stretch of letters from the word for rubbish

parts.note: offal is waste or rubbish
a set-to is a fight or argument

explanation.surface: A shrill row that breaks out over putting the bins out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is not a link word: 'taking out' removes OF from OFFAL to leave FAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a male singing voice pitched above the natural range.

clue.text: Thief wants to get new equipment on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to retool is to re-equip, as a factory does

explanation.surface: A burglar fancies some new kit on the return trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A looter steals goods, especially during unrest, so is a thief.

clue.text: Reduce status of cleric touring Middle East

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the cleric surrounds the region

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric

explanation.surface: A clergyman loses standing after a trip through the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity or standing.

clue.text: Africans take legal action to contain Britain's former settlers

indicators.note: to contain means the settlers are held inside

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action
the Danes settled in England in Viking times

explanation.surface: People in Africa suing over Britain's colonial-era settlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Sudan are Africans, an example of the category.
